subject: Encryption custody & rotation — detailed RFI responses for Acme Retail
messages:
From: John Doyle <john.doyle@acme-retail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Ops <security@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: encryption custody & rotation — starting list of clarifications

Hi Tessa / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick upload of the high-level RFI docs. We have a few follow-up clarifications from our security team to make sure we capture custody and rotation workflows properly in the evaluation: 

1) For customer-deployed private stacks — do you support connecting to a customer HSM (on-prem or cloud HSM) such that Redwood has zero access to the plaintext key material? If yes, what protocols (PKCS#11, KMIP, other) are supported?
2) For your hosted service, what is the default key custody model and which HSM providers/certifications do you rely on?
3) What is your recommended rotation policy and what tooling do you expose to run emergency rotations & rollbacks?
4) Are TLS certificates for control plane and customer endpoints auto-rotated? How do you handle OCSP/CRL for certificate revocation?

We’ve attached the Acme encryption tab in the RFI workbook — please paste short answers into the file if helpful. Also, we may want a short demo of the BYOK import + rotation flow.

Can we get your responses by EOD Tue (Feb 24)?

Thanks,
John
John Doyle
Head of Security Engineering — Acme Retail
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: John Doyle <john.doyle@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: encryption custody & rotation — starting list of clarifications

John — thanks for these focused questions. Below are concise, actionable answers we can paste into the RFI sheet; I’ve also attached an internal playbook that walks through the BYOK and rotation test steps (see attachment). If you prefer we can convert these to the spreadsheet cells and return.

1) Private / Customer HSM connectivity:
- Supported connectivity: PKCS#11 (Linux agent), KMIP (cloud HSMs like AWS CloudHSM and Vault HSM gateways), and a lightweight TLS-backed connector for on-prem HSM appliances.
- Custody model: When configured in Private mode with a customer HSM, Redwood operates in a "no-plaintext" posture: keys are generated/imported into the customer HSM and never exported in plaintext to Redwood instances. Redwood stores only key references/opaque handles and wraps payload keys with a customer-provided master key.
- Certifications: We validate integrations with FIPS 140-2 Level 3-capable modules commonly used by customers; for hosted HSM providers (CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) we rely on their validated modules.

2) Hosted service default custody:
- Default: Redwood-managed envelope keys stored in a cloud HSM maintained by our cloud provider partner. The envelope master keys are rotated by Redwood according to policy but are never stored as cleartext in long-term storage.
- Provider and attestation: We use a combination of cloud HSM and our hardware-assisted key cache, with regular attestation runs; customers may request a summary of HSM provider attestations under NDA.

3) Rotation policy & emergency rotations:
- Standard cadence: 90 days for envelope master keys; payload-data DEKs (data encryption keys) are rekeyed per session or by a 30–90 day cadence depending on workload.
- Tools: The Console exposes a rotation API and an operational playbook automating staged rotation (canary → full roll). Rotations are performed with a double-wrap technique to avoid downtime.
- Emergency rotation: We provide a fast-path API that rotates master keys and rewraps DEKs; the process is logged and auditable. Rollback is supported only when rotation metadata and cached key versions are present; full rollback to previous plaintext keys is not supported by design (no plaintext export).

4) TLS certificates & revocation:
- Control plane TLS: Certificates are provisioned from our CA or customer-supplied CA; we support automated rotation (ACME or customer-scheduled).
- Endpoint TLS: For customer-facing endpoints, we support both Redwood-managed certs (auto-rotate) and customer-provided certs. OCSP stapling is enabled for our endpoints and we integrate with customer OCSP/CRL feeds on Private deployments.

If helpful, Rishi can add a few lines about audit logs and the separation-of-duty controls. We can also run the live BYOK import + rotate demo during the call — I’m available Tue 24th morning PT.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-encryption-playbook.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Doyle <john.doyle@acme-retail.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: encryption custody & rotation — detailed notes on logging & ops

John/Tessa — quick add from an operations perspective: 

- Audit trail: Key lifecycle events (create/import/rotate/revoke/usage) are captured in our immutable audit log with key-hash references; log entries include actor, request id, and timestamp and can be exported to your SIEM (S3/Collector endpoint).
- Separation of duties: Key import/rotation requires dual-approval workflows in Dedicated/Private installs; hosted customers can opt-in to an approval flow enforced via RBAC.
- Access controls: Redwood engineers do not have default access to private key material for BYOK imports that are set to "customer-only". For hosted customers that opt for Redwood-managed keys, access is limited and audited by our security org.
- Key escrow/backups: For Private installs we support customer-controlled escrow snapshots (encrypted and stored in customer-controlled storage) — Redwood never holds escrow keys in plaintext.
- Testing: We recommend a staged rotation test — canary subset of endpoints, metric validation (latency/error rate), and health-check replays. The playbook attached to Tessa’s message includes the CLI commands and expected auditing output.

Let me know if you want a 30-min ops demo; I can run through an import + rotate from a simulated on-prem HSM in the sandbox.

-Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: John Doyle <john.doyle@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: RFI: encryption custody & rotation — detailed notes on logging & ops

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Can you confirm whether the hosted envelope keys use hardware-backed generation (HSM-backed RNG) in all regions?
- For the BYOK import flow in a Private deployment — do you support importing a pre-generated key blob (wrapped under a customer KEK) or only generation/import directly into the HSM?
- For the demo, we’d like to see: import, rotate, and emergency rotate; please include an example of the audit entries produced.

We are good for Tue 24th morning (we’re in PST) — can you send a calendar invite and DocuSign NDA for the attestation summary?

Thanks again,
John
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: John Doyle <john.doyle@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: encryption custody & rotation — demo + artifacts

John — great, we’ll run the demo Tue 24th 09:00 PT and bring the audit-output snippets. Quick answers up front: 

- Hosted RNG/HSM: Yes — envelope master keys are created with HSM-backed RNG in all our supported regions; we retain provider attestation copies for audits.
- BYOK import options: Private deployments support both direct import into the customer HSM (recommended) and import of a customer-wrapped key blob (we validate wrapping metadata and perform a non-exportable import into the HSM).

I’ve attached the playbook and a short checklist we’ll use for the demo. I’ve also included a DocuSign link for the attestation NDA (link below). Calendar invite to follow.

See you Tue —
Tessa
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
